newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand took a renewed battering on Thursday, losing over eight cents from its previous close at its worst intraday level following strong offshore and importer demand for dollars.
It ended a hectic, panic-stricken day at 4.7510/7560 on the dollar after an intraday low of 4.7550 reached in the late afternoon session and forex traders said further attacks were likely on Friday.
The rand's current all time low bid stands at 4.7670 reached on October 31.
"It's been a hell of a day... there was buying of dollars from all over," a senior forex trader said.
Traders were unable to give sound reasons for the heightened demand for dollars from offshore but said offshore speculators were active in the market.
There had also been strong local importer dollar demand in what one trader described as panic short-term covering before the festive break.

"The problem was that we did not have the same liquidity as in previous situations when the rand started sliding. The Reserve Bank was not in the market initially (when the rand started weakening), players panicked and that's when we saw the rand gapping the way it did," the trader said.
The central bank showed its hand later around the 4.74 level but dealers said the action had not been aggressive.
Dealers said it appeared the rand wanted to re-test its all-time high bid of 4.7670, noting that it was looking vulnerable to further attacks by speculators.
"It really all depends on the Reserve Bank tomorrow and to what extent it is prepared to intervene," one forex dealer said.
Others said that while a test of the 4.77 level looked likely there was also a lot of nervousness and uncertainty in the market which could cap the unit's losses at its previous all-time high.
Against the crosses, the rand also took a dive to last be quoted at 7.8520/8650 against sterling from 7.7367/7497 previously and at 0.3248/3252 marks from 0.3300/3304 marks.
Bonds also took a knock, breaking through the key 16 percent level during the morning as players sold stock on the back of a bearish undertone and the rand's woes.
At 1416 GMT the benchmark R150 bond was trading off its worst but weak at 16.135 percent from an intraday high of 16.15 percent and from 15.96 percent late on Wednesday.
"Bonds followed the rand which took many people by surprise... nobody thought it would weaken as much as it did," a bond trader said.

However, he believed the 16.15 percent level was toppish and the market should see some strength on Friday, possibly retracing back to around the 16.00 percent level with 15.98 percent a key level to break on the downside.
Bond Exchange statistics showed foreigners were net buyers of 89.99 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 13.46 million rand on Tuesday.
Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 2.11 billion rand on Wednesday from 1.48 billion rand on Tuesday.

On the money market, three-month NCD rates were quoted slightly higher at between 17.20 and 17.35 percent offered from 17.20 to 17.25 percent, while the 90-day BA rate also moved higher to between 16.65 and 16.95 percent from 16.55 and 16.90 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank indicated the money market shortage higher at 9.650 billion rand on Wednesday from 9.132 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Vera von Lieres, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
